title: Check the bench
prompt:
With your virtual environment active and the four tools installed, finish `bench.py` so it imports each tool under its usual short name and prints its version.

The tests check that the names `np`, `pd`, `plt`, `matplotlib` and `sklearn` exist in your file. Your version numbers can differ from anyone else's; that is fine.
hints: If the test says `No module named numpy`, your virtual environment is not active, or the install did not finish. Run `source .venv/bin/activate` in this terminal and try again.
The usual short names: `import numpy as np` and `import pandas as pd`. Matplotlib's plotting part is `import matplotlib.pyplot as plt`.
You need five import lines: `numpy as np`, `pandas as pd`, `matplotlib`, `matplotlib.pyplot as plt`, and `sklearn`. Then one `print` per tool.
explain_after: The short names are conventions the libraries' own documentation uses: `import numpy as np` [ml-018], `import pandas as pd` [ml-019] and `import matplotlib.pyplot as plt` [ml-020]. Everyone uses the same ones, so code you find elsewhere will read the same way.
